newsitem.title: USA: U.S. energy futures continue slide on ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. energy futures continue slide on ACCESS.

text.p: Prices for U.S. energy futures continued their daytime slide in after-hours trade Monday, with traders scrambling to sell after government data showed crude production would be higher than earlier forecast.
"I think people were thrown by the sell-off," one after-hours ACCESS trader said.

Prices should continue to fall on Tuesday, traders said, with players avoiding the market until the release of weekly inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute. November crude oil traded down 20 cents to $24.18 after falling 22 cents during the day, pressured by expiring October products futures.
November heating oil traded 70.25 cents a gallon, down about 0.50 cent from the settle on 92 lots traded.
October unleaded gasoline fell 0.26 cents to trade 62 cents a gallon on 100 lots.
October NYMEX products came off the board Monday, with traders rolling positions into November.
